subject: Data lifecycle sunset schedule and subprocessor assignments
messages:
From: Laura Singh <laura.singh@acmehealth.com>

Cc: security@acmehealth.com

Subject: Clarify Acme retention horizons and deletion proof (DPA/subproc)

Hi Kimberly / Marissa,

Thanks for taking this on. The legal team at Acme needs a clear, signed timeline for how Redwood will handle the following for our account before our audit next quarter:

- Backup snapshot lifecycle (how long snapshots are kept before permanent deletion)
- Log retention windows (app telemetry, request traces) and where short-term vs long-term logs live
- Subprocessor deletion handoffs (who deletes what and within what window once we request erasure)
- Evidence we can point to for deletion (subprocessor attestations, tombstone manifests)

I've attached a short spreadsheet with the items our counsel will check off (Acme_DPA_questions.xlsx). Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide: (1) a standard schedule we can reference in the DPA, and (2) an emergency/hold carveout process for legal holds?

Laura
Director of Security Operations
Acme Health
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Singh <laura.singh@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-03-21T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify Acme retention horizons and deletion proof (DPA/subproc)

Laura — thanks for the clear list and the spreadsheet. High-level answer up front, then next steps:

High level (proposed, negotiable in DPA addendum):
- Backup snapshots: standard retention 365 days for customer snapshots; after 365 days snapshots enter a 30-day tombstone phase before permanent deletion.
- Short-term logs (operational telemetry): 90 days rolling in hot storage.
- Long-term logs (audit/forensics): retained up to 2 years cold-backed storage by request (cost impact applies).
- Subprocessor deletion: Redwood instructs subprocessors to delete within 30 days of receiving a validated erase request; where a subprocessor requires a longer window we enumerate exceptions in the DPA annex
- Evidence: we can provide deletion manifests and subprocessor-signed attestations for deletions that cross subprocessor boundaries (template available).

Open items / Questions:
- Jordan, can you confirm the tombstone mechanics for multi-region backups and whether the 30-day tombstone is feasible for our current S3 lifecycle + Glacier setup?
- Marissa, procurement/legal: will Acme accept a 30-day subprocessor window or do they require faster confirmation? Also need approval for a Docusign amendment flow for the addendum.

I propose a short call tomorrow to walk Acme through the timeline and the evidence artifacts.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Singh <laura.singh@acmehealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-03-21T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify Acme retention horizons and deletion proof (DPA/subproc)

Kimberly / team — quick technical notes:

- Backup snapshot flow: we take regionally-scoped EBS/EFS snapshots and copy a catalog entry to our central metadata store. Current lifecycle policies support an archive-after-365-days transition and expire-after-395-days (matches the 30-day tombstone).
- Tombstone phase: during the 30-day tombstone we keep manifest metadata but mark blocks as 'scheduled-for-delete' so they are not used for restores unless we perform a recovery with legal sign-off. We then run a garbage-collection job that issues deletes to subprocessor stores.
- Subprocessors: for archival offload we work with two subprocessors (CloudVault and Nearline Partners). CloudVault accepts delete calls via API (can confirm 48-hour window); Nearline requires batch deletion scheduling (up to 14 days). That means the 30-day subprocessor window is realistic but may have per-subprocessor lag which we'll list as an exception.
- Evidence: we can emit a tombstone manifest (checksum list + delete command id) and request attestation receipts from subprocessors; we currently capture delete-job IDs in the audit log.

Action: I'll pull together a short runbook appendix (process, expected evidence bundle, and exception table) and post to Confluence. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Data+Lifecycle+Runbook

—Jordan
Principal Infra Engineer, Runtime

Thanks — a few compliance clarifications from Acme counsel's side:

- Legal holds: we need a documented hold lift / re-apply workflow; specifically a way to freeze deletes for a named hold and a labelled list of affected snapshots/log ranges.
- Proof: deletion manifests alone are fine if accompanied by subprocessor-signed attestations for cross-border subprocessors. Please attach your attestation template so counsel can verify the fields.
- Emergency erasure: clarify SLA for a high-priority erase request where data must be removed from accessible storage within 7 days. Is that operationally possible?

Attaching the attestation-template.pdf we typically ask subprocessors to sign. If you can draft a matching Redwood attestation flow that references subprocessor receipts we can close this out quickly.

Ellen
Compliance Advisor (external counsel)
